project.name: Knotz Raven Mayhem
project.productGoal: Make Knotz Raven Mayhem feel better than expected for a free GitHub Pages arcade game, especially for players testing on phones and installed PWA-style launches.
project.v1ScopeDecision: Local records and local progression only. Online leaderboards, databases, backend accounts, cloud saves, and service-worker/offline caching remain deferred beyond v1 unless explicitly approved.

handoffSummary.completedBaseline: The game is currently playable as a stage-grading arcade campaign with stage retry, dramatic grade reveals, S-rank confetti on the grading screen, run reports, armory upgrades, bosses, Jackpot Alley, local records, release shell assets, and GitHub Pages build support.
handoffSummary.nextTeamMission: Return to the mobile/PWA-first track. The next pass should make phone landscape, tablet, installed-app, and GitHub Pages testing feel deliberate, polished, responsive, and reliable rather than merely functional.
handoffSummary.qualityBar: A first-time tester opening the GitHub Pages link on a phone should understand orientation, start the game quickly, read the HUD, use touch controls comfortably, clear stages without layout overlap, and trust that the game is a real arcade build.
handoffSummary.latestKnownGate: npm.cmd run release:verify passed on 2026-05-28. It ran balance:report, build, release:check, and release:smoke. Release check signal: linkedAssets=3 seedAssets=4 releaseShellAssets=10 pwaManifest=ok. Dist smoke signal: basePath=/Knotz-Raven-Mayhem/ linkedAssets=3 seedAssets=4 releaseShellAssets=10 pwaManifest=ok.
handoffSummary.devServer: A Vite dev server has been used at http://127.0.0.1:5173/ for manual playtesting. Use npm run dev for local desktop checks, or npm.cmd run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5173 for same-network phone testing.
handoffSummary.handoffWarning: CI verification does not publish the live game. The GitHub Pages site updates only after the Deploy GitHub Pages workflow is manually run with workflow_dispatch on master.

currentPlayableBaseline.campaign: Nine authored stages are in place, including boss stages and Jackpot Alley. The player advances through the arc using grade and star pressure instead of lives-based failure.
currentPlayableBaseline.stageGrades: Missed non-bonus ravens become escaped grade-eligible enemies. Stars are awarded from grade percent: 5 stars at 90%+, 4 at 80-89%, 3 at 70-79%, 2 at 60-69%, and 1 below 60%.
currentPlayableBaseline.stageRetry: Stage clear now includes Retry Stage so players can replay the current stage from its checkpoint and improve the score, coins, grade, and star outcome for that stage.
currentPlayableBaseline.gradePresentation: Stage transition presentation now emphasizes the grade more than the percent. S-grade clears trigger the DOM-overlay S RANK text and confetti on the grading screen itself.
currentPlayableBaseline.runReport: Quitting from pause or stage clear banks rewards and shows total stars, average grade, perfect stages, coins, and armory recommendations.
currentPlayableBaseline.progression: Recovery Matrix preserves the internal thickJacket save id and adds a small grade buffer per rank. Grade Shield preserves the extraLife powerup id but now forgives one grade-eligible escape per charge.
currentPlayableBaseline.localPersistence: Save version remains 1. Existing local saves should keep working, including prior thickJacket ranks.

mobilePwaBaseline.currentDirection: Landscape-first mobile remains the accepted direction for v1. Portrait currently acts as an orientation gate rather than a full portrait gameplay layout.

manifest.note: Relative manifest paths are intentional for GitHub Pages base-path safety.

mobilePwaBaseline.htmlShell: index.html includes viewport-fit=cover, theme color, manifest link, apple-mobile-web-app-capable, apple-mobile-web-app-title, apple status bar styling, and social preview metadata.
mobilePwaBaseline.cssShell: src/styles.css owns safe-area variables, touch-action controls, portrait orientation gate styles, and short landscape viewport rules.
mobilePwaBaseline.releaseShell: public/ owns icons and social preview assets. release:check currently expects releaseShellAssets=10 and validates the PWA manifest contract.
mobilePwaBaseline.offlineCaching: No service worker or offline caching is currently approved for v1. Do not add caching semantics without an explicit product decision and a stale-asset invalidation plan.

nextTeamPrimaryFocus.name: Real-device phone landscape fit and touch feel
nextTeamPrimaryFocus.goal: Make the game feel intentionally designed on common iPhone and Android landscape sizes, not just shrunken desktop. Validate HUD density, stage-clear controls, run report, armory, pause/options, and touch target comfort.

nextTeamPrimaryFocus.name: PWA installability and GitHub Pages path safety
nextTeamPrimaryFocus.goal: Confirm installed launches, relative manifest paths, icons, splash/background colors, standalone display, and the /Knotz-Raven-Mayhem/ base path continue to work after every mobile change.

nextTeamPrimaryFocus.name: Grade and retry UI on mobile
nextTeamPrimaryFocus.goal: The new grading screen is now a core feature. Ensure the dramatic grade reveal, Retry Stage, Continue, Quit Run, stars, reward math, and S-rank confetti remain readable and usable on phone landscape.

nextTeamPrimaryFocus.name: Mobile performance and effects budget
nextTeamPrimaryFocus.goal: Protect framerate during boss stages, dense raven waves, screen shake, DOM confetti, S-rank celebrations, and mobile browser compositing. Add caps or reduced-effect behavior if real devices show jank.

nextTeamPrimaryFocus.name: Release QA and deployment confidence
nextTeamPrimaryFocus.goal: Keep the local gates green, update the release checklist with concrete phone/PWA cases, and preserve the manual Deploy GitHub Pages workflow path.

recommendedFirstSprint.outcome: Ship a mobile/PWA polish pass that can be tested from both the local LAN dev server and the public GitHub Pages URL.
steps: Audit current phone landscape at 667x375, 740x360, 844x390, 852x393, 932x430, and at least one tablet landscape size.
Fix any overlap or cramped controls in HUD, stage clear, S-rank grading screen, run report, armory, pause/options, and portrait gate.
Tune touch affordances and hit targets so the game can be played without accidental taps or obscured action.
Validate installed PWA-style launch behavior on at least one iOS and one Android device where possible.
Confirm GitHub Pages build output still uses the correct base path and relative PWA shell paths.
Update DOCS/RELEASE-QA-CHECKLIST.md with the exact mobile/PWA cases that were actually run.

mobileQaChecklistForNextTeam: Open the local LAN dev server on a real phone in landscape. Expected: no browser chrome or safe-area overlap blocks HUD, controls, stage-clear buttons, or run-report actions.
Open the public GitHub Pages URL on a phone after deployment. Expected: assets load from /Knotz-Raven-Mayhem/, no blank screen, no missing icon/social/manifest assets.
Rotate to portrait during menu and gameplay. Expected: the orientation gate is clear, polished, and recoverable when returning to landscape.
Install or add to home screen on iOS and Android where available. Expected: standalone launch uses the correct title, icon, theme/background color, orientation, and start URL.
Start a fresh Stage 1 run with touch input only. Expected: movement, firing, pause, and menu actions feel reachable and do not fight page scroll or browser gestures.
Miss several Stage 1 ravens, then finish the stage. Expected: no lives failure, escaped count rises, grade percent/stars drop, and stage clear still fits on phone landscape.
Use Retry Stage from stage clear. Expected: the same stage restarts, previous attempt values do not double count, and the next clear can improve the stage result.
Clear a stage with S rank. Expected: grade reveal and confetti happen on the grading screen, do not hide primary actions, and do not tank framerate on a real phone.
Use Continue, Retry Stage, and Quit Run from the mobile stage-clear screen. Expected: all three actions are visible, tappable, and visually distinct.
Open the Run Report from Quit Run. Expected: totals, stars, average grade, perfect stages, coins, and action buttons fit without scrolling traps or overlap.
Open Armory on phone landscape. Expected: upgrade text, prices, purchase affordances, and preserved Recovery Matrix rank remain readable and usable.
Play or simulate boss stages 3, 6, and 9 on a phone. Expected: boss health/readability, projectile pressure, boss-spit minis, and grade HUD remain understandable.
Play Jackpot Alley. Expected: bonus-round labeling and payout fit on mobile, and missed bonus enemies do not lower stars.
Toggle reduced shake or other options where available. Expected: mobile users can reduce intense effects without breaking feedback.
Try a repeat visit after deployment. Expected: no stale asset or cached-manifest behavior creates a blank screen or old build confusion.

githubPagesDeploymentNote.currentStatus: Local release verification was green after the grade conversion. The correct publish path remains manual Deploy GitHub Pages on master after mobile/PWA manual QA is acceptable.
githubPagesDeploymentNote.why: The classic Pages branch/folder source can show a blank white screen after the Vite migration because it may serve stale or mismatched static output. The Actions deployment uploads the freshly built dist artifact.

doNotChangeWithoutApproval: Do not add online accounts, backend saves, databases, leaderboards, or analytics without approval.
Do not add a service worker or offline caching without an explicit cache invalidation and GitHub Pages stale-asset plan.
Do not replace the current grade/stars/stage-retry progression model while doing mobile polish.
Do not make portrait gameplay the main v1 mode unless the product direction changes.
Do not remove the relative manifest/start_url/scope behavior without proving GitHub Pages deployment still works.
openQuestionsForMobileTeam: Should v1 remain landscape-only with a premium orientation gate, or should portrait menus become a later supported mode?
Should installed PWA launch hide any browser-only instructions or add a dedicated first-run touch calibration prompt?
Do the current touch controls need larger zones, configurable sensitivity, or a different phone layout?
Should S-rank confetti and heavy VFX automatically scale down on low-end phones?
Should the final Stage 9 clear receive a special end-of-arc recap before any future overflow or endless-stage work?
